turn2.differences: The author's conditions match my step one reading closely. The one soft spot is the contract condition: none of the files literally have the word contract in their name, so it functions as a contextual type judgment rather than a strict keyword match, which is how a careful reader would naturally interpret it.

ambiguity_effects.explain: Read literally as requiring the word contract in the filename, zero candidates match. Read descriptively as a PDF that functions as a contract, record 8101 an MSA clearly qualifies. Most careful readers converge on the descriptive sense since it is the only workable reading, but the initial hesitation is genuine.

Every description that mentions Initech and renewal at all contains the exact phrase Initech renewal verbatim in records 8101, 8103, 8104 and 8105. Record 8102 mentions neither word under any reading, so the literal versus conceptual distinction does not change which files pass.
Record 8103 at 1,950,000 bytes fails under both decimal and binary interpretations. Record 8104 at 2,600,000 bytes passes under both. No candidate sits in the zone where the two units would disagree.
Every comment record in the dataset is a top-level comment with no replies, so counting top-level comments only versus counting all comments gives identical totals for every file.

turn2.naturalness_note: The request stacks several technical filters in one sentence, reading more like a precise disambiguation query than casual speech, but it is plausible as a real request from someone using an assistant to pick one file out of several similarly named documents.
